matchups.recap:
Harley Jarvis scraped out his Canoeing Masters this week, 116.06 to 113.7, on the strength of Ashton Jeanty running like a woodsman running to the camp store for 25.4 and C.J. Stroud turning in a Guide Rec of his own at 20.46. Good thing those two showed up, because Ja'Marr Chase had his lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow, managing a measly 5.6 against a 21-point projection, and Isaiah Likely added to the gloom at 4.0. Call it Blue Ridge's tug of war — won, but nobody's framing the box score.

Omarion Did You Know ran this week's activity bushwhacking without a compass at the quarterback position, riding Kirk Cousins's 7.4 while Jonah Coleman carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 32.9 and Travis Kelce chipped in 22.4. Tank Dell and Jaylen Warren both walked on the alpine vegetation, combining for 8.1 points on a projected 23.37, and the whole cabin is left wondering what might have been. Chalk this one up as poor preparation meeting a counselor who simply read the week better.

This week's canoe trip down the scoreboard came down to a paddle-length, Catalina Wine Mixon edging Funk that Junk by 4.24 in a real tug of war. Patrick Mahomes carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 24.96, and George Pickens and Mike Evans both turned in Guide Rec outings, enough to cover for DK Metcalf's stunned naval battle queen impression at 0.7 and Cam Skattebo quietly ate his trail cheese and salami at 4.3. Call it preparation, call it luck, either way the Chair Force found just enough arrows for the bullseye.

Funk that Junk had the horsepower — Cam Ward's 22.22 and a matched set of 17.5s from Breece Hall and Bucky Irving — but Emeka Egbuka Stole my wow with a measly 2.8 against a 9.03 projection, and that gap was the whole ballgame. Old balls ran a respectable camp activity otherwise, but one Beak outing from the receiver room left this cabin bushwhacking without a compass down the stretch, and Catalina's counselor earns the sticky buns on Sunday morning for it.

away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
Paralegal ran a pig and back at the backfield this week, letting Chuba Hubbard and Jahmyr Gibbs carry the load like a pair of Woodsman Chiefs on the same hike, 26.0 and 25.8 respectively, while the 49ers D/ST chipped in 14.0 just to make the math embarrassing. Luther Burden III did his best impression of a Dutch Oven, managing only 2.3 on a 12.4 projection, but with that kind of production up front, 55 Burgers still cruised to a well-earned Tuna Casserole and a Guide Rec for Counsel's weekly planning.

Babysitter of little children 2014 got a Boss showing from Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey, but the man whose name is on the cabin, Chase Brown, spent the afternoon like living on the Point, scraping together 6.1 on a 13.16 projection. That kind of lead-foot performance from your namesake back is hard to recover from, and Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare never found the footing to make this a tug of war, falling by 19.34 and heading home to patch up the lineup before next week's hike.

Team Bradford, still living up to the Campcraft Enthusiast tag, ran a pig and back of a week despite handing the ball to Courtland Sutton and watching him turn in a full-blown Dutch Oven, 0.0 points on a near-nine-point projection. No matter — Emmett Johnson carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 22.3, DJ Moore chipped in 19.1, and Derrick Henry kept grinding like a woodsman running to the camp store all afternoon. The margin got a little tighter than it should have, but 100.1 points papers over a lot of Beak.

The Machine Knows, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back, dropping a second straight and showing no real feel for the week. Javonte Williams went off for 22.6 and Malik Nabers added 15.0, but Josh Allen's 12.16 was strictly living-on-the-Point stuff, and the whole operation never found its footing. Bradford's cabin earns the sticky buns on Sunday morning while the Machine counselor heads back to the drawing board — again.

Chef Boyardee ran this one like a man who already knew the weather forecast. Dak Prescott threw for 35.9 and carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike, Tetairoa McMillan and Devaughn Vele chipped in without drama, and even with Jonathan Taylor ate his trail cheese and salami at 4.7, The Goose is Loose had all the arrows in the bullseye en route to a 96.1 showing. Call it Stefanowitz-approved preparation, however you want to misspell the name on the cabin roster.

Ricky Huns, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back for a second straight week, Bushwhacking without a compass behind a trio of zeroes and near-zeroes — Xavier Hutchinson, Kyle Monangai, and J.K. Dobbins combined to give back nearly ten projected points apiece worth of nothing. Kittle, Williams, and Barkley tried to drag the canoe themselves, but the rest of the roster was Stuck in the Sewards, and the losing streak just keeps writing itself.

The Island Gudge posted 74.8, which on most weeks is a perfectly respectable showing at this camp, but Love Thy Naber had other plans and torched the scoreboard for 111.56. CeeDee Lamb went like a woodsman running to the camp store with 24.7, Jayden Daniels chipped in 17.06, and James Cook III carried his share — the whole operation had all the arrows in the bullseye. This was the largest margin of victory across all of camp this week, so Flame On, I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF.

The Gudge got a genuine Guide Rec from Joe Burrow's 19.9 and Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 14.7, but Bhayshul Tuten, Garrett Wilson, and Jordyn Tyson all walked on the alpine vegetation, combining for barely more than Lamb scored alone. That's gonna need to patch those holes with more leaves territory. No fault of the plan here — the dice just landed Beak side up, and the Island Gudge will be back on the trail next week.

headline: Week 11 wraps up with upsets and lopsided scores
